dispositions.reason: AC-7 as approved (no copy of the secret anywhere in process memory) cannot be met or tested in Node; the plan substitutes a weaker hash-purge property, and only a SPEC amendment can decide what AC-7 should actually require.

The SPEC does not state whether a rotated key in its grace period keeps admin and key-management rights; this is a product intent question (rotation as a leak response) that no plan can settle without a SPEC decision.

The plan must say that rotate's 'must be active' check and the idempotent-revoke check go through keyState (status-less keys read as active; an expired but unpurged rotated key reads as expired), or the seeded test keys would 409 and break AC-1/2/3/6.

The plan must stop settling alone whether the last admin key can be revoked: either declare a guard or state it as an explicit accepted bound for the human to confirm; unsure the plan can stand as written, so it goes back.

The plan must declare the purge failure paths: whether a failed request-start purge is skipped or fails the request, and that the interval purge catches and handles its own rejection so it cannot crash the process.
The plan must state as a limit (and in the README) that a v3 data file cannot be loaded by the previous release and that purged or revoked hashes are gone for good, so downgrade is not supported.

The plan's choice to write no audit entry or log for grace-end expiry and hash purge conflicts with the README rule that state changes are audited; it must either add an entry or justify the exception against that convention for the human to confirm.

The plan's risk text claims key ids are shown to admins only, but the id is part of every token (tl_<id>_<secret>); that claim is wrong and must be corrected, and the key-state disclosure either accepted explicitly or the check order changed.
The plan must state how rotateKey creates the new key (reusing createKey would write key.created) and that key.rotated is the last audit entry written, otherwise AC-6's newest-entry check fails.

README completeness is a minor documentation improvement; the plan already lists a README step with endpoints, errors and a rotation paragraph, and the build can name the Deprecation header and new fields there without a plan change.

Only the word 'guarantees' in a risks paragraph is off; the AC-7 mapping already says the purge is unit-tested on the document, and the wording will be revised anyway when the AC-7 question goes back to the SPEC.
